articles.body: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has been at home, spending some quality time with his wife, Lauren Kyle, after a brutal season on the ice in the last season. Just days ahead of the new season, Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle has shared a rare update about their lives.Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle opens up what the two are busy with ahead of the new seasonA few hours ago, Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle took to her social media as the high profile couple hosted a bunch of close friends at their place.While one picture shows the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain Connor McDavid playing a game of chess with his friends, another one shows him and his wife sitting down to have dinner with their friends.The caption of the picture reads as, “Last dinner in this house forever…”For now, it has not been confirmed if Connor McDavid and his wife, Lauren Kyle, are moving to a new place, ahead of the new season.After the last season ended, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain Connor McDavid has mostly kept himself out of the spotlight as he spent his time recovering during the offseason.Connor McDavid reflects on the new season for the Edmonton OilersWith just days left for the new season to begin at the end of September, Connor McDavid opened up about in an interview with Bleacher Report.The Edmonton Oilers’ star player said, "There's always excitement opening night…The first game of the season is always so highly anticipated and there's so much excitement. And then obviously opening night, to be a part of that is something we haven't had a chance to do in the last number of years, there's something to be said to play on that night.”The popular captain added, “It means a lot, everybody's watching. I know I've been at home watching opening night and seeing the first look at the new season. It's an exciting night and something that we're excited to be a part of, and hoping to get off to a good start."Connor McDavid continued, “Everybody can play, right from the best teams in the league right down to the teams that are vying for the first overall pick. It's tough every single night. We got our work cut out for us, we know that. We gotta build our program back to the standard that we think it needs to be at, and we'll do that. articles.title: LSU alum Ben McDonald says he doesn't agree with NFL-to-college returns, but understands why coaches want them
articles.summary: Former LSU Tigers star Ben McDonald said he opposes ex-NFL players returning to college, but he understands why Lane Kiffin wants every edge to win.
articles.body: As the LSU Tigers prepare for their season opener against the Clemson Tigers, not all eyes are focused on the current matchups to expect in Death Valley. The college football world is waiting to see if tight end Dae’Quan Wright, as well as former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, among others, will be available to play for LSU after causing quite the controversy by reuniting with Lane Kiffin at the NCAA level after being released by the Cleveland Browns following a training camp stint with the NFL team. Even as college football's Week 0 has passed, the debate continues over a growing trend: former NFL rookies and other athletes attempting to move from the professional ranks back to college in pursuit of a fifth year of eligibility. The SEC and other major conferences have pushed back on new guidelines, but injunctions and temporary restraining orders issued by local judges have generated a series of court proceedings and strained relations among the NCAA, conferences, schools and others. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Ben McDonald, the first overall pick of the 1989 MLB Draft, Olympic gold medalist, and former LSU Tigers star pitcher, appeared on "America Reports" where he told Sandra Smith about his stance on the current stir running through the college ranks. "Personally, I don’t believe in it," McDonald explained. "I think once you get to play your four years, for me, it’s time to move on at that point. But things are so different now when you talk about the NIL money and the money that’s out there now, you get why these kids want to come back. "So, if you can’t make it in the NFL, MLB, wherever, maybe you have that opportunity to return for a fifth year of college and make some money. You don’t blame the players for wanting to continue to play. They love the sport, they want to continue their athletic career. But also, money is involved." MATT RHULE SOUNDS ALARM ON NFL RETURNEES, $45 MILLION ROSTERS AND COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S PAYROLL PROBLEM One of the NFL’s top agents, Drew Rosenhaus, who also represents Wright, explained why he supports players returning to college if they are within the current "5-for-5" rule set by the NCAA in June, which gives student-athletes five years of eligibility to play five seasons. For one, as McDonald mentioned, there’s the financial perks of returning to college rather than sitting on a practice squad for NFL rookies. "He is not going to make an NFL team this year," Rosenhaus said on "One Nation with Brian Kilmeade." "At best, he would be on a practice squad. He feels playing another year in college would be great for his development, and it will allow him to get bigger, stronger, more experienced and take another shot at the NFL. Oh, by the way, he would make more money in college than he’d make on an NFL practice squad." Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule recently appeared on OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich," where he added how much of a boost players like Wright got already because they’ve gone against pros in an NFL training camp. "Twice as good," Rhule said about Wright’s development having been with the Browns. "I think the hardest thing when you’re coaching these guys, you’re always telling them, ‘Hey, do this. This is what it’s like at the next level.’ It would be at least twice, if not three, times better than they were." So, in that respect, McDonald understands a coach like Kiffin wanting to go after these players wishing to get back to college. "Whether you agree with it or not, if I’m a college coach and I have the opportunity to get a kid that’s got four years of college experience, and he was in an NFL training camp, why would I not want him to come back to my roster? It only allows us a better chance to win," he said. "Everybody’s picking on Lane Kiffin because it’s low-hanging fruit for him. There’s been a lot of controversy over Kiffin lately, leaving Ole Miss and the great year he had the last few years at Ole Miss, and now he’s the head coach at LSU. But it’s not an LSU thing. This is across the board. …I don’t totally agree with it, but I understand where it’s at right now. And if I’m a head coach, hey, I want those players. There is pressure to win now, and why not get the best players you can?" NFL WARNS CLUBS THEY CANNOT SIGN ANY PLAYER WHO RETURNS TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL FOR 2026 SEASON, MEMO SAYS McDonald added the other side of the argument, believing "it hurts our incoming freshman class because those kids don’t have really nowhere to go with the 5-for-5 deal that’s out there right now." Kiffin said that he spoke with his players’ leadership committee, where they were at a consensus to "bring ‘em" into the program if it meant winning this season. "We understand we have a team that's practiced together and worked together all offseason, but one of them said, 'Hey, this is how it works at the next level, and this is how the real world works.' So, that made me feel a little better in the struggle and being torn back and forth," Kiffin told reporters on Monday. Kiffin’s final roster is due to the SEC on Friday, which is the day before the team will take on Clemson. On Thursday, a judge in a Louisiana courtroom will either uphold the temporary restraining order, which would prohibit the SEC from punishing schools if they were to add a player like Wright, or reverse the decision after hearing from the SEC and NCAA following a show-cause order. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Elsewhere in the SEC, coaches like Texas’ Steve Sarkisian opposed the idea of bringing back players that went pro. "The fact that somebody out there is going to take a player off of an NFL roster and tell somebody who's been doing it for nine months to go kick rocks, that doesn't sit well with me. I think that's wrong. That, morally, is wrong," he said, via ESPN.

articles.title: From watching Shin-chan, Doraemon and K-dramas to translating shuttlers' words for the world: How young interpreters found their way to badminton's biggest stage
articles.summary: Badminton News: NEW DELHI: At the recently concluded BWF World Championships, players weighed every word as carefully as their drop shots. But beyond the glare of the.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At the recently concluded BWF World Championships, players weighed every word as carefully as their drop shots. But beyond the glare of the cameras, another contest was quietly unfolding. Standing a step behind the athletes were the interpreters, almost invisible yet carrying the immense responsibility of ensuring that nuance survived the journey from Mandarin, Japanese or Korean into English.At a World Championships, where every word can travel as quickly as a smash, a mistranslated phrase can soften conviction, distort the meaning of an entire exchange or, in the worst case, trigger an unintended geopolitical controversy. For the interpreters, getting the words right is only part of the job. The real challenge is ensuring that nothing gets lost in translation.Chaavi Raj, one of the three Mandarin interpreters, felt the pressure immediately when local hope Ayush Shetty stunned World No. 1 and defending champion Shi Yu Qi in the opening round."There was a lot of pressure. There were so many media houses present. My first match was with Ayush Shetty. China lost. It was a big upset," explained the third-year PhD student in Chinese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University.For the 29-year-old Raj, it was a daunting first assignment. He had worked for businesses, exhibitions, tourists and ministries. Sports and media were new territory.Like India, where there are multiple dialects, Chinese also changes with region, context and tone. It was difficult in the beginning. It is a pictographic language. You have to memorise it. This is the challenge of Mandarin.Raj, who hails from Bihar's Sitamarhi district, has been studying the Chinese language for five years and travelled to Beijing for a visiting scholarship. After his first preference, Spanish, did not materialise, he shifted his focus to Mandarin, graduating in Chinese Language and Culture Studies."Like India, where there are multiple dialects, Chinese also changes with region, context and tone. It was difficult in the beginning. It is a pictographic language. You have to memorise it. This is the challenge of Mandarin," he explained."It is a tonal language. If the tone changes, the meaning changes. It is very easy to forget. It is difficult to memorise. We watch videos to keep ourselves in touch. We watch web series and movies. We talk to our Chinese friends. We do all this to stay in touch with the language," he added.The BWF brought three interpreters of its own to the tournament, while the Badminton Association of India (BAI) recruited three more through a PR firm and a third-party vendor.Sahin Parween and Nandini were two of the other interpreters roped in by the BAI. Parween, a recent graduate from JNU's School of Language, Literature and Culture Studies, was first intrigued by Japanese culture while watching animated series such as Doraemon and Shin-chan. Her interest was reinforced later in life as anime found its feet in India. The fact that Japanese is a high-paying language in India has also played a role, she admits almost sheepishly."We are paid between Rs 4,000 and Rs 10,000 per day. Korean and Japanese generally pay better if you compare them with Western languages. The rate can even go up to $200 (Rs 19,000) or more," says Parween, who graduated just a month ago.When we found out the tournament was happening, we searched what it was about. Then we searched for the vocabulary and the questions the media could ask. Then we prepared for what the players could reply to those questions.Like Parween, Nandini's route to Korean was similarly shaped by pop culture. After picking up the language in 2018, her interest was piqued by K-pop and K-dramas. Perhaps unsurprisingly, language was already part of her life: her father speaks 13 Indian languages.Still relatively new to the profession, the duo spent days training ahead of the World Championships, which returned to India after a gap of 17 years."When we found out the tournament was happening, we searched what it was about. Then we searched for the vocabulary and the questions the media could ask. Then we prepared for what the players could reply to those questions. Still, there was some nervousness," explained Nandini, who is a third-year BA student of Korean Language and Culture.Before the World Championships assignment, they would chip in when ambassadors or exchange students visited JNU. Both also make the most of opportunities to meet Japanese, Korean and Chinese people as part of university discussions.This, however, was a different challenge altogether."There is a lot of pressure when you know that the player is relying on you solely. When the question is asked, they look at our faces, and it's up to us. And we have to explain it in the right way," says Nandini.For the youngsters, the pressure was complicated by another fact: they were often interpreting for players they admired."At the same time, we are also their fans. We just blank out sometimes because we are very busy processing, okay, 'we are seeing them in real life'. Also, it happens in interpretation that when something is asked or said, we may know the word but we just blank out because of nervousness. So, we find another way to say it," she said."There are times when we feel like we could have done better. We have moments where we are unsure of the most appropriate word. But at the end of the day, we are also learning," she continued.We see the videos beforehand, the interviews they have given in Chinese. Then we prepare the words. We see which words can be used well. We also take the help of AI. We give prompts asking the tool to go through the videos and suggest which words and vocabulary are repeated most often. Sometimes we write it down, sometimes we make notes.Choosing the right word can be the difference between a routine interview and a diplomatic incident. During the Cold War, disputed translations of Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev's remarks and a notorious mistranslation of US President Jimmy Carter's 1977 speech in Poland became famous examples of how a few misplaced words can distort meaning.Mandarin interpreter Chaavi Raj understands the importance of every word in his preparations. His PhD studies focus on China-US relations and the perception of former American diplomat and Secretary of State Henry Kissinger. He prepares by studying archival footage of the players' previous interviews. Increasingly, AI tools have become part of that preparation."We see the videos beforehand, the interviews they have given in Chinese. Then we prepare the words. We see which words can be used well. We also take the help of AI. We give prompts asking the tool to go through the videos and suggest which words and vocabulary are repeated most often. Sometimes we write it down, sometimes we make notes," Raj explains his process."It is very important to do it right. In such a big event, where there can be a diplomatic incident, you cannot take a chance," he says while showcasing his notebook full of Chinese characters, or Hanzi.By the time the last microphone is lowered and the player disappears towards the lounge, the interpreters have already faded into the background. Their names rarely make the broadcast or the byline, yet every headline, quote and television soundbite owes something to their precision. In a sport decided by millimetres, theirs is another game of fine margins: finding the right word, preserving the meaning and making sure nothing gets lost between the player and the world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Nothing went according to my plans’: K Humpy opens up ahead of Olympiad title defence
articles.summary: Chess News: K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Nor did she say that.
articles.body: K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Nor did she say that she would play according to the wishes of the team or captain. But she dropped enough hints.“I have played a few Olympiads and have always played on board one. For many years, we have been following the rating procedure for maintaining the board order. I don’t know how they are going to look at it this year,” Humpy told TOI from Vijayawada on Monday. Top seeds India are set to defend their gold medal in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, starting Sept 16.Humpy finished eighth with 3.5 points in the nine-round classical Cairns Cup in St Louis, USA. But her Norway Chess campaign in May-June, where she finished sixth and last, was particularly disappointing. “It’s not so comfortable to enter into the Olympiad in such a scenario,” said Humpy. “I'm just waiting to get back in good shape. I was a bit rusty but it happens to every player. You’ll be in that bad phase and then you’ll come out of it.”On her poor run in Norway, Humpy said, “I played the tournament after a very long gap. Nothing went according to my plans. This year was disturbing. I was also a bit upset with the off-the-board things and probably that also reflected in the way I played.”Humpy withdrew from the Candidates tournament in Cyprus after FIDE turned down her request to shift the eight-player women’s world championship qualifier to a safer venue, citing security concerns arising from the war in West Asia.“I think I’m fine now,” she said. “Probably, it did disturb me for a few months. Like, it’s not easy for a player who has been professional and working towards it and then taking all the negativity. So it did affect me. I spent many sleepless nights as well. But for the last month or so, I have been in better shape.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cam Smith, Nelson Velázquez deliver key blows in Astros' win over White Sox to start tough stretch
articles.summary: In the beginning of a stretch of 13 straight games against potential playoff teams, the Astros came through with a big win over the AL Central-leading White...
articles.body:
The Houston Astros got key hits from Nelson Velázquez and Cam Smith to start strong on a tough stretch of games that could decide their fate in the American League West.

The Astros beat the Chicago White Sox 6-3 Monday night at Daikin Park in the first of 13 straight games against potential playoff teams with National League wild-card contenders Arizona Diamondbacks coming to town after the White Sox (72-65), who lead the AL Central, followed by a road trip to play likely NL wild-card team Philadelphia Phillies and Tampa Bay Rays, who have the best record in the American League.

The win pushed the Astros' record against opponents who are .500 or better to a Major League-best 26-14 (.650). They maintained their two-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West and increased the lead over the Seattle Mariners, the defending division champions, to six games. Houston also climbed within 2 ½ games of the White Sox for the second seed in the postseason, which comes with a bye past the wild-card round.

The Astros (70-68) trailed 2-1 with two outs and nobody on in the bottom of the fourth inning. After Smith sparked something with a triple, Velázquez delivered his first hit since the Astros claimed him off waivers three weeks ago , a two-run homer that banged off the barrier just below the train tracks in left field.

Smith helped add to the lead in the following inning. After singles by Christian Vázquez, Yordan Alvarez and Isaac Paredes loaded the bases, Christian Walker brought home a run with a walk to make it 4-2 Astros. The White Sox opted to pull starter Anthony Kay after he struck out Daulton Varsho so righty Trevor Richards could face Smith. It didn't work. Smith ripped a 2-2 changeup down the left-field line for a two-run double and a 6-2 lead.

The Astros got the scoring started in the third in an inning that began with Nick Allen reaching on a throwing error by third baseman Miguel Vargas. When the Astros put runners on the corners with one out, Alvarez hit a ground ball to second that looked like it had a chance to be an inning-ending double play, however Alvarez beat out the throw to first, allowing Allen to score the game's first run.

Given a small lead, Peter Lambert struggled mightily in the fourth, an inning which he needed 30 pitches to complete. After retiring the leadoff hitter, Lambert allowed the next three hitters to reach with a Colson Montgomery double, a Chase Meidroth RBI single and a hit by pitch from Tristan Peters. After striking out nine-hole hitter Jake Rogers, Lambert walked Sam Antonacci to load the bases, then walked in a run with a walk to Munetaka Murakami that put the White Sox up 2-1.

The Astros' bullpen of Enyel De Los Santos, Bennett Sousa, Steven Okert and Bryan Abreu combined to give up just one run on two hits in the final 4 ⅓ innings.

Lambert wasn't able to make it through five innings for just the second time in his past 12 starts. The 29-year-old right-hander walked a season-high five batters, which pushed his pitch count up. By the time he walked Colston Montgomery with two outs in the fifth, he had thrown 104 pitches and was removed.

Lambert, who needed 30 pitches to complete a fourth inning that included two walks and a hit batter, allowed two runs on three hits and five walks with six strikeouts in 4 ⅔ innings.

Lambert, who didn't make the Astros' opening day roster, leads the team in wins (8), starts (24), innings (132 ⅔) and strikeouts (131).

Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez added to his RBI total with a ground ball in the third inning to give him 94 RBIs, which leads the American League. Alvarez also leads the league in average and is tied for the lead in home runs, putting him on track for the Triple Crown. The Tigers' Miguel Cabrera won the Triple Crown in 2012, but before him it hadn't been done since Carl Yastrzemski's 1967 season. Alvarez's .317 average is six points ahead of the Rays' Chandler Simpson in second place. Alvarez is tied with Tampa Bay's Yandy Diaz with 37 home runs and has a three-RBI lead over the Orioles' Pete Alonso.

Astros fans have hated the Mauricio Dubón-for-Nick Allen trade ever since former general manager Dana Brown made it in November. Allen has been on a heater to make the trade look far more even than it did when it was considered mostly an offseason salary dump.

In 78 games, Allen, who went 1-for-3 Monday, is hitting .277 with a .684 OPS. Dubón, who is making $6.1 million and can become a free agent this offseason, is hitting .268 with a .700 OPS in 131 games for the Atlanta Braves.

Allen, who is making $1.4 million and still has three more years of team control, has hit .349 (15-for-43) since the All-Star break.

articles.title: ‘Thank God That QB Is Gone’ — Colorado HC Deion Sanders Beyond Grateful For Not Having to Face Former Georgia Tech Fan Favorite Haynes King
articles.summary: While the NFL regular season is rapidly approaching, college football has already kicked off. While Week 0 is in the books, Deion Sanders’ Colorado Buffaloes...
articles.body:
While the NFL regular season is rapidly approaching, college football has already kicked off. While Week 0 is in the books, Deion Sanders' Colorado Buffaloes are still preparing for their first game.

With Colorado kicking off their season on Thursday against Georgia Tech, Sanders is already discussing the Buffaloes' upcoming opponent and how thankful he is that quarterback Haynes King is gone.

Deion Sanders Glad He Won't Have to Face Haynes King

Speaking to the media on Monday, Coach Prime took time to share his appreciation for Georgia Tech's Brent Key, whom he called a " hard-nosed, detailed " head coach. Sanders realizes that Thursday's matchup will be a "tremendous challenge" for a Buffaloes team that went 3-9 last season.

"Hard-nosed, detailed coach," Sanders said. "It's gonna be a tremendous challenge. But I love it. I absolutely love it. New parts of his staff that are phenomenal. Guys that come from the professional level as well from the collegiate level. They're playing a big role for them this season."

Georgia Tech, meanwhile, finished last season with a 9-4 record, including a 27-20 win over Colorado in the season opener. While showing respect for his opponent is noteworthy, Sanders' best soundbite came when he heaped praise on the "difference-maker" Haynes King, whom Colorado will no longer have to face.

"Thank God that quarterback is gone," Sanders added. "That kid. That kid refused to lose a year ago, and he was definitely a difference-maker. I think he had what, a buck-forty rushing? One-fifty-six? Thank you for checking me. I wanted to settle at 140. Yeah, this is a great team though, man."

Sanders was close. King ran the ball 19 times for the aforementioned 156 rushing yards and 3 touchdowns while completing 12-of-20 passes for 143 passing yards and an interception.

King is now on the Carolina Panthers, and he made the team's initial 53-man roster as an undrafted free agent after starring during the preseason.

While Sanders is glad that he doesn't have to game plan for King anymore, as he noted, Georgia Tech will still present a challenge. The Yellow Jackets will be starting Alberto Mendoza, who transferred from Indiana and is the younger brother of Fernando Mendoza. Last season, Mendoza threw for 286 yards, 5 touchdowns, and 1 interception while also rushing for 190 yards and 1 touchdown.

Sanders is clearly very thankful that the Buffaloes no longer have to deal with King running up and down the field, but Mendoza is no slouch either.

articles.summary: After being let go by FOX Sports, Joy Taylor has been receiving quite some criticism on the internet. And it’s mostly because of her monthly maintenance rema...
articles.body:
After being let go by FOX Sports, Joy Taylor has been receiving quite some criticism on the internet. And it's mostly because of her monthly maintenance remark. Many fans blasted the demand as out of touch. However, former NFL running back and ex-FOX analyst LeSean McCoy, who was let go after the network canceled his show The Facility , had a different opinion.

"This is my thing when they talk about going broke," McCoy told his co-hosts on the Speakeasy podcast . "Giving your girl $5,000 a month… Like, what bills you really paying? First of all, if y'all live together, those are your bills too, dude. You going to pay for groceries, you going to pay the car, you gonna pay all. You don't pay all that anyway.

"All these athletes, you're not going broke by giving your mom some allowance and giving your girl allowance. When you go broke, when you got five cars, you're flying private when you want to… Now, for me, I'm paying it."

The debate began when Taylor claimed that a hypothetical $5,000-a-month allowance wasn't enough for her as a stay-at-home partner, saying that about $2,500 a month would easily go toward her personal maintenance and upkeep. She framed the extra savings as a financial cushion in case the relationship ended, and she had to start over.

"The $5,000 is completely doable if you live a certain type of way, if you are a certain type of woman," Taylor said on the Two Personal Show . "If you're very, very, very low-maintenance, y'all could do it. But don't come over here with that."

Netizens bombarded Taylor with harsh backlash. They accused the media star of promoting unrealistic financial standards and expecting too much from a provider. But McCoy's perspective highlights a different note altogether.

That said, Joy wished to advance her career in broadcasting.

"I am diving into producing," Taylor revealed during an interview with Front Office Sports . "So I started my career as a producer. When I started at FAM, my first job in the business was as a producer."

She confessed that she loves making things for other people and being behind the camera. She pointed to the many interesting stories in sports that she believes still deserve to be told, acknowledging the demand for those stories. That interest is part of why producing has become a focus for her next chapter. To make things work, she even launched The Daily Play in May 2026. That's where she tries to tell the sports stories in just five to ten minutes.

Nevertheless, the discussion is still an open-ended one. But do let us know what you think of LeSean McCoy's opinion.

articles.title: Keon Sabb Is Playing His Best Football Yet, and That Should Terrify Alabama’s Opponents
articles.summary: Armed with championship experience and unwavering consistency, the veteran safety anchors a secondary aiming for national dominance while evolving into the c...
articles.body:
There might not be another position group on Alabama's roster that I am more excited to watch this season than the secondary. And there might not be another player in that secondary more important to what Alabama wants to accomplish defensively than Keon Sabb .

We have talked all offseason about how talented this Alabama defense can be. We have talked about the returning veterans, the young talent, the depth and the expectations surrounding Kane Wommack's unit. But when you start looking at the pieces Alabama has on the back end of the defense, it is easy to understand why expectations are so high.

Bray Hubbard is one of the best safeties in college football. Zabien Brown has already shown that he can be an elite cornerback. Alabama has continued stacking talent in the secondary through recruiting. Then there is Sabb. The veteran safety is healthy, experienced, confident and, according to Alabama defensive coordinator Kane Wommack, playing the best football he has played yet.

That is a pretty scary thought for the rest of college football. Back in March, Sabb was asked just how good Alabama's secondary could be in 2026.

Four words. No hesitation. No complicated answer. And I love it.

Because this Alabama secondary should have that type of confidence. There is a difference between being arrogant and understanding the talent inside your own locker room. Sabb has been around enough good football players to know what a great secondary looks like.

He played at Michigan before transferring to Alabama. He has played against elite competition. He has been around NFL-caliber players. He understands what championship-level football looks like. So when someone like Sabb says Alabama has the ability to have the best secondary in America, I listen. But Sabb also knows that saying it in March means absolutely nothing if Alabama does not prove it once the season begins.

That is where his role becomes so important. Sabb is not simply another talented defensive back. He is one of the leaders of this entire football team. Kalen DeBoer recently described Sabb with one word that I think tells you almost everything you need to know about him.

"I love consistency," DeBoer said. "That is one of the words that applies to Keon, and that I love about him. He's been consistent from day one. You know what you're going to get from him." That might not sound like the flashiest compliment in college football, but I actually think it is one of the best compliments a coach can give a player.

Coaches want players they can trust. They want players who prepare the right way when nobody is watching. They want players who understand the defense, communicate, make adjustments and do their job snap after snap. That is Sabb.

DeBoer also praised Sabb's intelligence and his ability to process what is happening on the football field.

That matters tremendously at safety. A great safety cannot simply be athletic. He has to understand formations. He has to recognize tendencies. He has to communicate with the rest of the secondary. He has to understand what the offense is trying to accomplish before the ball is even snapped.

One mistake on the back end can turn into six points very quickly.

Sabb has reached the point in his career where Alabama can trust him to see the bigger picture.

He is not simply reacting anymore. He is processing. He is anticipating. He is leading. And maybe most importantly, he is teaching the younger players around him how to do the same thing.

Sabb understands that part of being a veteran means preparing the next generation of Alabama players.

"As an older guy, I feel like it's definitely my job to continue to preach what my coach is preaching as well," Sabb said.

He explained that whatever the coaches are teaching him, he tries to pass along to the younger players because eventually they will be the ones leading the program. That tells you everything about the type of teammate Sabb has become.

College football has changed tremendously. The transfer portal has changed roster management. NIL has changed recruiting. Players have more opportunities than ever to move somewhere else when things become difficult or when they believe another situation might benefit them.

Sabb could have left Alabama. He could have entered the NFL Draft. A lot of people expected him to. Instead, he looked at himself and apparently believed there was still more football left inside of him.

More development. More improvement. More to prove.

That decision could end up being one of the most important decisions for Alabama's defense this season.

Sabb's first two years in Tuscaloosa were not exactly normal. He transferred from Michigan ahead of the 2024 season while Alabama itself was going through one of the biggest transitions in college football history.

Nick Saban retired. Kalen DeBoer arrived. A new coaching staff came in. A new defensive system was installed. Everybody was adjusting. Then Sabb suffered a broken foot against Tennessee in 2024 that ended his season. And while he returned the following year, Wommack believes the effects of that injury were still there.

"I think if you ask him, he was probably still physically battling some of that injury from 2024," Wommack said. "It lingered a little bit." That is something fans sometimes forget when evaluating players.

Being cleared to play does not always mean being completely healthy. There is a difference between being available and being yourself. There is a difference between getting through a football game and playing completely free without thinking about an injury. Sabb spent much of last season trying to work his way through the aftermath of that foot injury.

For the first time in several years, he has had something close to a normal offseason. No transfer. No learning an entirely new program. No major injury recovery dominating his preparation.

Just football. Training. Studying. Getting stronger. Improving his technique.

And Wommack believes we are seeing the results.

"He's grown fundamentally. He's grown physically," Wommack said. "His maturity and the way he carries himself has been really impressive, and he's aged like a fine wine." Wommack eventually delivered the line that should have Alabama fans extremely excited heading into the season.

"I think he's playing his best football right now." That is exactly what Alabama needs.

Sabb himself mentioned improving his footwork and lateral movement as one of his biggest offseason focuses. Those small improvements can make a massive difference for a safety. A fraction of a second matters. One cleaner change of direction matters. One better angle matters. One step can be the difference between breaking up a pass and allowing a touchdown.

For Sabb, this offseason was not about reinventing himself as a football player.

It was about sharpening everything that was already there. The instincts. The intelligence. The physicality. The experience. The leadership. And now Alabama appears to be getting the most complete version of him yet.

That should also make life easier for everyone around him. A veteran safety who understands the defense at a high level can help settle an entire secondary.

He can help young corners get lined up. He can recognize what an offense is trying to do. He can communicate adjustments. He can cover mistakes. He can give Wommack more confidence to disguise coverages and become aggressive because he knows the players behind the front seven understand exactly what is happening. That is why Sabb's value cannot simply be measured by interceptions or tackles.

His biggest impact might be everything Alabama avoids because he is on the field. The busts that do not happen. The coverage mistakes that get corrected before the snap. The younger player who gets pointed in the right direction. The communication that prevents a receiver from running uncovered down the field.

Those things rarely appear in a box score. They win football games anyway. And then there is the NFL conversation.

Sabb returned to Alabama because he felt there was still another level he could reach. Right now, some projections have him as a later-round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. I would not become too attached to those projections. If Sabb really is playing the best football of his career and Alabama's secondary becomes what many of us believe it can become, his draft stock could rise quickly. NFL teams love experienced defensive backs who can communicate, process information and play multiple roles. Sabb has already shown plenty of those qualities. Now he has an opportunity to put together a healthy, complete season and remind everyone why he was such a highly regarded player in the first place.

Right now, Alabama has much bigger goals. This football team enters the 2026 season with something to prove. The Crimson Tide are talented, but talent at Alabama has never really been the question. The question is whether this team can take all that talent and turn it into championship football.

If Alabama is going to get back where it wants to be, the defense has to be great. Not good. Great.

And the secondary might have to lead the way.

That means Sabb will be right in the middle of everything. I also think his story represents something important about this Alabama roster under DeBoer.

Development matters. Patience matters. Adversity matters.

Sabb did not have a perfect first two seasons in Tuscaloosa. He battled an injury. He battled through recovery. He could have gone to the NFL. He could have decided his college career had already shown enough.

Instead, he came back. He went to work. And apparently he has become an even better football player because of it. That is the kind of veteran presence Alabama needs when championship expectations are returning to Tuscaloosa.

There will be talented freshmen who need guidance. There will be difficult road environments. There will be moments when the defense gives up a play and has to immediately respond. There will be fourth quarters when experience matters.

Those are the moments when players like Sabb become invaluable.

Alabama does not need him to be Superman. It needs him to be exactly what DeBoer described him as.

Consistent. Smart. Dependable. Prepared. A great teammate. And if Alabama gets all of that while also getting the most physically prepared and technically refined version of Sabb we have seen?

Then maybe those four words he said back in March will become reality.

There is still a lot of football to be played before Alabama can earn that title. But when you have players like Hubbard and Sabb patrolling the back end, along with the ridiculous amount of talent Alabama continues to collect in the secondary, you certainly have a chance.

And Sabb might be entering the season at exactly the right point in his career. Healthy. Experienced. Motivated. And playing his best football yet.

For Alabama, the timing could not be better.

articles.title: Padres second baseman Luis Rengifo will have season-ending surgery for a torn ACL
articles.summary: The Padres announced Monday that imaging showed a full tear of the ACL. The injury had initially been diagnosed as a knee sprain.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — San Diego Padres second baseman Luis Rengifo will undergo season-ending surgery for a torn ACL in his right knee.

The Padres announced Monday that imaging showed a full tear of the ACL. The injury had initially been diagnosed as a knee sprain.

Rengifo was injured in the seventh inning of a 7-6 loss to Tampa Bay on Saturday when he threw across his body toward home and fell to to the infield dirt. Rengifo needed assistance getting to his feet before he was driven off the field in a medical cart.

The play happened when two Tampa Bay players were near third base at the same time and Cedric Mullins broke for home. Rengifo was chasing Taylor Walls when he made the throw and immediately went down.

Rengifo started the season with the Milwaukee Brewers, who released him on June 23. He hit .205 in 57 games with the Brewers.

The 29-year-old appeared in 38 games for the Padres, hitting .292 with four homers.

articles.title: Bills Add Ex-Browns First-Round Selection to Practice Squad
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills added a former Cleveland Browns draft pick to their practice squad on Monday after final roster cuts. The post Bills Add Ex-Browns First-Ro...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills added 17 players to the practice squad on Monday, and one of them was a 2020 first-round pick.

Buffalo signed left tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. to the practice squad after the Chicago Bears released him on Sunday.

Wills Spent Five Seasons With the Cleveland Browns

The Browns drafted Wills to be the team's starting left tackle, but he didn't have the best five years in Cleveland.

First off, the Browns moved Wills from right tackle to left as a rookie. Wills played right tackle at Alabama, and a big part of that decision was that he protected Tua Tagovailoa's blind side, since he is a left-handed quarterback.

Wills played in 58 games for the Browns, but he struggled to stay on the field during the last two seasons. The Browns made the playoffs in 2023, but Wills was absent for most of the run due to a season-ending right knee injury he suffered in Week 9 during a win over the Arizona Cardinals at Huntington Bank Field.

The next season was worse for Wills, as he played only five games, starting four, after aggravating the knee injury he suffered the season prior.

Wills was a free agent all of last season, and he didn't want to sign with a team because he wanted to take care of his knee injury.

"I injured a couple of ligaments, but usually when people like when they get fell on or something in their knee, they mess up all their ligaments and people can just go in and repair it and they get healthy," Wills said in March, via Zack Pearson. "I had minimal damage to my ligaments. It was more of an alignment issue from where I got fell on. So they had to actually – it wasn't my knee, they had to go into my femur and do what was called an osteotomy to kind of correct my alignment. So my knee is healthy."

The Bears took a chance on him this offseason, but they must've not liked what they saw from him in training camp and the preseason because he couldn't make their 53-man roster.

Buffalo doesn't need Wills to play at all this season unless injuries occur on the offensive line. If the Bills don't need to see him in any games, then maybe letting him sit out a year on the practice squad could be beneficial. This would let him practice a full season, potentially helping him develop into a reliable backup swing tackle next year.

There is a chance that another team could come in and steal Wills from the practice squad and sign him to their active 53-man roster this season. Bills fans should be on the lookout for this.

articles.title: Sean McAdam: Red Sox’ returnees Trevor Story, Roman Anthony making sudden impact
articles.summary: It hasn't taken long for Trevor Story and Roman Anthony to make big contributions after missing several months.
articles.body:
BOSTON — The goal, the credo, for those in the medical field is well known: First, do no harm .

In a way, it's the same for athletes returning from long stints on the sideline. Players coming back from injuries don't want to be disruptive or interrupt the momentum that their team may have built in their absence.

As such, Trevor Story and Roman Anthony have tried to rejoin the Red Sox as inconspicuously as possible, quietly returning to their posts without calling too much attention to themselves.

While Story was recovering from surgery to fix a sports hernia and Anthony was recuperating from a finger/wrist issue, the Red Sox found some life, executing a U-turn that lifted them from last place to playoff contention. And now that they're healthy again and have reclaimed their spots on the roster, they'd prefer to just blend in, thank you very much.

But through two games, that hasn't been the case. On Sunday in Yankee Stadium, they each collected two hits and looked like they hadn't missed any time. Monday night, back home at Fenway, they took things to another level.

Anthony reached base three times, scoring the tying run in the ninth inning after leading off the inning with a gift triple, badly misplayed by Seattle center field Julio Rodriguez.

Meanwhile, Story cranked a two-run double high off The Wall in the eighth to pull the Red Sox to within a run, then lined a game-winning, walk-off single to left-center in the bottom of the 10th sending his team to a thrilling 9-8 win over the Mariners.

The scorecard for the duo after two games: eight hits, three runs scored and three RBI.

"They look good. They look really good," said interim manager Chad Tracy. "Both of them, their at-bats were good....Both of them have swung the bat really, really well."

Anthony's return has been somewhat more seamless, as there was little doubt he would become an everyday presence in the lineup, either in left supplanting an underperforming Jarren Duran or at DH, a season-long black hole for the club even when Masataka Yoshida was healthy.

Compounding matters was the fact that Story had struggled at the plate before he went to the IL. Could he reasonably lay claim to the everyday shortstop job?

"That was the biggest thing about the rehab — making sure that with this group and what they've done, for Trevor and I, that when we come back, there's no hiccups," said Anthony. "I felt good about where I was at coming into (Sunday) and just going to continue to ride it out."

As electric as his ninth inning triple was, Anthony capped it with an artful slide home, getting his hand around catcher Cal Raleigh and evading the tag with a nifty swim move.

As pleased as he was with his own exploits, Anthony was even happier for Story.

"Getting to go through this process with him, I'm so happy for him," said Anthony. "Every at-bat, he continues to look better and better. He's just a true veteran. He's the same guys every day, good or bad, and to see him do (what he did tonight) was unbelievable."

Story's eighth inning Wall-scraper plated two, and as the bottom of the 10th unfolded, it became more and more likely that he would have the opportunity to play the ultimate hero. The Mariners, in fact, made sure of it when, after a bunt moved ghost runner Eli White to third, they elected to intentionally walk both Caleb Durbin and Jarren Duran to load the bases.

Was Story even more amped up that the Mariners filled the bases to get to him?

"Yeah, yeah," said Story, a sly smile creasing his face. "For sure."

That both Anthony and Story were the night's biggest stars in their first home game back wasn't lost on Story.

"It means a lot," said Story of the night. "We've been watching from afar for a while, just supporting the boys and thinking about the time when we can get back on the field and contribute. We'd talk about it a lot and just be looking forward to that. Here we are, and it's been fun."

Story made sure to credit the environment at Fenway for lifting the players' performance.

"This atmosphere kind of brings out the best in you," he said. "It's as simple as that."

Story knew he risked expecting too much from himself upon his return, of placing undue pressure on his own shoulders.

"For me, always, that's usually better for me, is trying to do less," he said. "It's not about us coming back to do anything other than fit in and try to win games."

Monday, he and Anthony, his summer rehab partner, more than did their part.

articles.title: Steelers news: Omar Khan hopes Joey Porter Jr. finishes his career in Pittsburgh
articles.summary: Pittsburgh General Manager Omar Khan kept a tight lip while talking about Joey Porter Jr.’s contract negotiation. He refused to go into specifics of the neg...
articles.body:
Pittsburgh General Manager Omar Khan kept a tight lip while talking about Joey Porter Jr.'s contract negotiation . He refused to go into specifics of the negotiation, but he did mention that Porter Jr. will hopefully finish his career in Pittsburgh.

"We won't talk publicly about the negotiations per se, but Joey knows how we feel about him, and I still hope Joey finishes his career here. Our policy is going to remain in place, but I'm not going to talk about negotiations," Khan said.

Irrespective of where things stand between the two parties, Porter can still practice with the team and play the regular-season games.

"In the next couple of weeks, not just Joey, but anyone that we feel is healthy and available to us, we expect him to practice. He got taken off [PUP]. Our medical staff felt like he was good to go," Khan added.

Though the Steelers also have a philosophy of their own , which many call "hardline deadlines and zero in-season negotiations." The Steelers cut off the contract negotiations at the beginning of the season. According to them, the focus should remain on football during the regular season.

So technically, the Steelers' front office has a short window to sign Porter if they want to offer an extension. While there are roster options to fill the position, the team has until Week 1 to decide the cornerback's future.

Additionally, the Steelers received a positive update on the injured wide receivers DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, as well as safety Jaquan Brisker. All of these players are expected to suit up for Week 1, as reported by ESPN.

However, veteran safety DeShon Elliot would not suit up against the Atlanta Falcons for Week 1.

articles.title: Sloppy defense costly, Yankees open West Coast trip with 10-1 loss to Angels
articles.summary: The Yankees were blown out by the Angles in the opener of a three-game set Monday night in Anaheim.
articles.body:
The Yankees were defeated by the Los Angeles Angles 10-1 in the series opener on Monday night.

Elmer Rodriguez put together his best big-league outing to this point his last time out, but the Angels were able to take advantage of some ineffectiveness this time around. The youngster held them off the board in the first and the second, but two out hits in the third and fourth chased him from the ballgame.

All in all, he allowed four runs on four hits, three walks, two HBP, and five strikeouts over 3.2 innings.

The Yankee offense was held in check by Walbert Ureña over the first four-plus innings, but Spencer Jones provided them with some much-needed life, crushing a one out solo homer deep over the right-center wall in the top of the fifth to cut into the four-run deficit.

The youngster is up to eight home runs on the season, five of which have been over his last 30 games.

Michael Fulmer and New York's defense immediately gave that run back to the Angels. Christian Moore blooped in an RBI double that bounced away off of a sliding Jones' glove in shallow right, then scored a run of his own as a pair of throwing errors on a pickoff attempt brought him in from second.

Fulmer was charged with his first earned run across six outings since joining the Yankees.

Luis Gil was also hurt by the Yankee defense in his first MLB appearance as a reliever. Gil struck out three in his first frame, but not before Jose Caballero committed his second error in as many innings, forcing him to throw more pitches and bringing in LA's seventh run of the game.

Gil followed that with a scoreless second inning, working around a one out HBP.

David Bednar was called upon for the eighth inning in a six-run game, and he was roughed up pitching for just the second time over the last 10 days. Bednar gave up three runs, two of which scored on a Vaughn Grissom double, which gave him three hits and four RBI in the ballgame.

Coming into the night, Bednar had allowed just two runs (one earned) in August.

Other than Jones' homer the Yanks weren't able to get much else going against Ureña. The righty held them to just that one run on five hits while walking none and striking out eight batters across seven strong innings. His ERA is down to 2.85 during his impressive rookie campaign.

With the two miscues from Caballero, the Yanks lead MLB in errors from the shortstop position (39).

The youngster continued his great rookie season with seven innings of one-run ball.

Gerrit Cole (7-7, 3.19 ERA) takes the ball against Grayson Rodriguez (4-5, 6.03 ERA) in the middle-game on Tuesday at 9:38 p.m.

articles.title: Cubs news: Clay Holmes loving offense after bonkers run support vs. Brewers
articles.summary: Clay Holmes must be loving life after the Chicago Cubs acquired him in a trade from the New York Mets. Going from a team that’s been underperforming througho...
articles.body:
Clay Holmes must be loving life after the Chicago Cubs acquired him in a trade from the New York Mets. Going from a team that's been underperforming throughout 2026 to one that has a legitimate shot at winning a World Series title has to be reinvigorating, and it has to do wonders for Holmes' confidence to see the Cubs' offense show up every single night.

On Monday, the Cubs popped off for 17 runs in a 17-3 blowout of the Milwaukee Brewers — with the team hitting nine home runs in a single game, breaking their previous franchise record. Chicago didn't even need Holmes to be perfect from the mound, but he was still brilliant, holding the Brewers scoreless in six innings of work, allowing just five hits and two walks while striking out eight.

The Cubs' offense has been unreal in August; they scored 178 total runs this past calendar month, leading MLB, and they hit a league-best 62 home runs on their way to doing so — hitting 20 more long balls than the second-best team (the Cincinnati Reds hit 42 dingers in August). Suffice to say, the morale is quite high right now in the Cubs locker room, and Holmes is reaping the rewards of their high-octane offense as well.

"It's an impressive group … tonight they broke an all-time record for homers in a month … the energy it takes to show up every day and play defense the way they do. They're slugging the ball … It's August and they're showing up with the same energy. It's not an easy thing to do," Holmes said in his postgame presser, via Marquee Sports Network on X.

Everyone is showing up for the Cubs. Holmes has an ERA of 1.55 in five starts (29.0 innings) for the Cubs since arriving at the deadline. This team needed excellent pitching to complement its high-powered offense, and this is the way they need Holmes to pitch from here on out if they were to make it deep into the postseason.

articles.title: Why people are overreacting to Savannah State's 87 point loss
articles.summary: Perhaps the biggest story this week happened in a game many weren’t even paying attention to. Chennis Berry and the reigning HBCU champion South Carolina Sta...
articles.body:
Perhaps the biggest story this week happened in a game many weren't even paying attention to. Chennis Berry and the reigning HBCU champion South Carolina State Bulldogs opened their season at home against Savannah State. Aside from Savannah State being Chennis Berry's alma mater, there was nothing truly important to note. South Carolina State was expected to win and win big. But no one expected 87 points.

South Carolina State's dominance was awe-inspiring. They were simply bigger, quicker, faster, and more skilled than South Carolina and Savannah State's new unit under first-year head coach Thomas Howard. Everything seemed to click for the Bulldogs throughout the matchup. Jokes about the score spread quickly across social media, and understandably so. But the tone of the conversation around the game shifted to a place where things stopped being funny.

Many sports fans unfamiliar with HBCU football started using Savannah State's showing as an indictment of the program and a way to say change was needed, even though change had already happened with Thomas Howard's hire. Some people spread lies about Savannah State, even though they didn't know the Tigers moved back to the SIAC and Division II athletics in 2019. The rhetoric started to become destructive and even conspiratorial at certain points, with allegations of Berry being turned down in interviews with Savannah State and the loss being a debt repaid for being overlooked, festering.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

When HBCU stories break containment, Misinformation starts to happen, and the institutions involved get hurt, so we have to set the record straight.

In all honesty, Savannah State should not have been playing South Carolina State in Thomas Howard's first game leading the program. A lot of people have limiting views of Division II football, treating it as a sub-quality subdivision of college football instead of giving it the reverence that it deserves for producing some of the best players in both the FCS and FBS. Some of the best Division II programs have challenged and tested solid Division I programs so much that some schools no longer schedule specific Division II programs. The classification of Division II is not a scarlet letter.

But Savannah State simply is not equipped to match up against the HBCU national champion of Division 1. Between scholarship allocation and experience, they were outmatched and likely should have played an out-of-conference Division 2 opponent, such as other teams in the SIAC, or potentially an FCS opponent more in line with Savannah State's trajectory as a program. Lost in the conversation about the 87-point win is the fact that Chennis Berry-led teams are just that good.

To the uninitiated, South Carolina State's dominance over the Tigers is a blight on Savannah State's football program, but many have to understand the history that Berry has made over the past few seasons. Below is a snapshot of some of his signature victories during his time at Benedict and South Carolina State.

South Carolina State (2024 & 2025 seasons)

Chennis Berry is creating the resume of an HBCU coaching legend. He has multiple conference championships. He now has a Celebration Bowl victory under his belt. All he truly needs is an FBS victory over a Group of Five program and potentially a successful appearance in the FCS playoffs to truly cement his legacy in HBCU football. It already is cemented in many ways, which is why the result of Saturday's game should shock no one.

In his two coaching stops, Chinsbury orchestrates these types of victories. He recruits the players that can resoundingly overpower programs that don't have the same level of talent. He gets his teams to believe and ultimately finish the job and not play up or down to their competition. They play consistently at every point. South Carolina State itself is a model of consistency in HBCU football.

From Willie Jeffries, Bill Davis, Buddy Pough, and now Chennis Berry. The program is the epitome of excellence in HBCU football. The program has produced four Pro Football Hall of Fame members and countless other NFL standouts, such as Shaquille Leonard, Javon Hargrave, and Cobe Durant. South Carolina State is the standard, which is again why this win isn't shocking.

When FCS HBCUs lose to teams like Ohio State, as Grambling did last season, it's widely understood why. No one called for the firing of Micky Joseph for losing 70 to 0 early last season. They just accepted it as it was, and Joseph moved on to have a phenomenal season, improving their record from the 2024 season. Why can't the same reverence be given to a dominant program like South Carolina State and a transcendent coach like Berry?

Losing to South Carolina State isn't a reason that Thomas Howard should be fired or proof of a failing football program. While the loss was indeed bad and there's no defending 87 points, proper context needs to be applied for the betterment of Savannah State and their ability to recruit players in the future.

South Carolina State is the equivalent of Ohio State and other dominant, championship-winning programs in the HBCU football space. If you don't come correct, you might as well stay home, and that's what all the folks talking about this game need to understand.

articles.title: Phenix City 12U All-Stars return home from Little League World Series
articles.summary: PHENIX CITY, Al. (WRBL) — The Phenix City 12U All-Stars captivated the community over the past few weeks, and on Monday night, that community turned out in f...
articles.body:
PHENIX CITY, Al. ( WRBL ) — The Phenix City 12U All-Stars captivated the community over the past few weeks, and on Monday night, that community turned out in force to welcome the team home.

Hundreds piled into field 8 in Idle Hour Park to celebrate the accomplishments of this little league team, in search of autographs and pictures with the young superstars.

Both players and coaches spoke with WRBL during Monday's celebration. Head coach Case Rasmus said he wasn't surprised by the large turnout, noting that the community had supported the team every step of the way.

"I'm really not surprised," Rasmus said. "The community has been with us this whole trip. They've followed us through social media, emails and text messages, and they've shown up everywhere we've played, from Warner Robins to Pennsylvania."

And the community took one more opportunity to show up for this team on Monday night, celebrating the history made by this team. This year's squad is the first from Phenix City to make it to Williamsport, with the 1999 squad winning the U.S. Championship.

articles.title: ‘Thought He Was Gonna Get Fired’ — Ex-NFL Scout Gives ‘Credit’ To Bill Belichick for Being ‘Unfazed by Chaos’
articles.summary: Bill Belichick’s stint at North Carolina has not gone according to plan, as Year 1 featured ton of chaos and losses. However, North Carolina pulled off a 15-...
articles.body:
Bill Belichick's stint at North Carolina has not gone according to plan, as Year 1 featured ton of chaos and losses.

However, North Carolina pulled off a 15-10 upset of TCU in Dublin in Week 0 to silence his doubters. One year after the Horned Frogs embarrassed UNC 48-14 in Belichick's college debut, the Tar Heels flipped the script and got revenge. Now, former NFL scout John Middlekauff is praising Belichick for thriving amidst UNC's chaos.

John Middlekauff Praises Bill Belichick's Ability To Ignore Chaos

"Everyone thought they were going to get their [expletive] kicked," Middlekauff said on his "3 & Out" podcast before pointing to what he considers one of Belichick's defining traits.

"He's so unfazed by chaos," Middlekauff said. "You do got to give Belichick some credit, though, when everybody, and I mean everybody, universally thought he was going to get fired in mid-season."

Middlekauff has seen that quality before. He referenced the New England Patriots' 2007 Spygate season, when Belichick's team went 16-0 in the regular season despite the scandal dominating the early part of the year. To Middlekauff, the pattern is less about eliminating distractions than operating normally while they pile up.

To Middlekauff's point, Belichick entered Year 2 under serious pressure after North Carolina went 4-8 in 2025. PFN highlighted a preseason resignation prediction that had Belichick leaving in November if the Tar Heels fell to 2-7, while ESPN's Heather Dinich discussed the possibility that he could retire.

However, with North Carolina winning the opener against TCU, that noise has quieted down. UNC won thanks in large part to their defense, with Belichick handling the defensive playcalls since his son, Steve, is currently on medical leave.

TCU went ahead 10-3 with four minutes left in the first quarter and did not score again. UNC forced three turnovers on downs, recovered a fumble, and held the Horned Frogs scoreless for the final 49 minutes. The Tar Heels' 2026 Defense Impact Score now sits at 89.1, which ranked second-best among the teams that played in Week 0.

"And definitely in this game, didn't think he had a snowball's chance in hell," Middlekauff said in the clip . "And he went over there and kind of dictated the terms of the game. Got to give a guy a little credit."

That credit comes with obvious limits after one game. North Carolina's offense produced only 15 points, and the 4-8 season that created the pressure around Belichick did not disappear in Ireland.

Still, the contrast with last September is difficult to miss. TCU once turned Belichick's college debut into a 34-point humiliation. Twelve months later, UNC kept the same opponent off the scoreboard for nearly three quarters and left Dublin 1-0.

For Middlekauff, it served as the latest evidence that chaos has rarely altered Belichick's pulse.

articles.title: Manchester City, Chelsea in talks at last over potential Enzo Fernández deal — reports
articles.summary: Here we still could go
articles.body:
As we head into the final day of the transfer window, the Enzo Fernández situation remains unresolved. It's only been going on for the whole summer, after all (if not longer), so there's been hardly any time to get it done, right?

Our (former?) Vice-captain has been training with the team, but he's been held out of our first three games, either at his own request or by the coach's decision or by the sporting directors', or by a combination of all. Chelsea tried to set a deadline before the start of the season for Manchester City (or any other team) to bid, but all that's done is make it even more frustrating that we're still in limbo. That deadline was then retconned to be a deadline for "bids of (at least) £120m", which just means that we now have to talk about a fee as well.

But, at long last, we are actually talking, club-to-club through official channels, as per all the usual talking heads at the transfer rumor mill content farm, like Fabrizio Romano and David Ornstein, and all the rest.

Whether these talks will lead to anything here on the final day is anyone's guess. Romano is just playing up the drama as usual, but Ornstein, speaking on BBC Sport , claims that Chelsea would only really consider doing business if we could somehow come out ahead not just in the books but on the pitch as well. And that would mean getting someone in to replace Enzo in some way, shape, or form. But links with Lamine Camara of AS Monaco, Manu Koné of AS Roma, and Alex Scott of AFC Bournemouth have all led to the same narrative dead end, and now there's hardly any time left.

Forcing players to stay is never a good idea, but sometimes it's not the worst thing.

articles.title: Peyton Watson Explains Why Kyrie Irving Is The Toughest Player He’s Ever Guarded
articles.summary: When naming the toughest player he ever had to guard, Peyton Watson explained what made Kyrie Irving a tough cover.
articles.body:
Peyton Watson is widely regarded as one of the most promising young wings in the NBA. Although this year's offseason was marked by prolonged contract talks and the inevitable drama that follows, Watson now finds himself in a new environment after being traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers .

While joining the Cavs could be a phenomenal opportunity for Peyton Watson, it is worth acknowledging his time spent with the Denver Nuggets . Having established himself as an elite two-way player over the 2025-26 season, Watson's credibility as a versatile defender undoubtedly boosted his overall stock.

Because of his ability to guard multiple positions, Peyton Watson has often faced some of the league's best offensive players. Thus, when asked who he considered the toughest player to guard on a recent episode of the " Curious Mike " podcast with Michael Porter Jr. , Watson had to give a shout-out to one of the league's most creative scorers.

"Definitely, Kyrie Irving is on top of that list," Watson stated. "Bro, because you can literally just play perfect defense and he's just a basketball savant. He's got the most sophisticated and most refined game that I feel like I've ever seen."

"That's one of those guys that you look at and say, and I use this all the time, but the best of the best, bro, their talent is in their fingertips," Watson continued. "It's like he touches that ball, and he's just like a painter with an open canvas, and they're just out there playing like it's art, and Kyrie's one of those guys. Super tough to guard."

Kyrie Irving 's reputation as an offensive player often precedes him. While boasting arguably the best handle in NBA history, Irving is also an immensely versatile scorer. From elite footwork and three-point shooting to an incredible layup package, including off-hand finishing, many attest to Kyrie Irving's scoring ability .

Given that Irving didn't play during the 2025-26 season, Peyton Watson may have faced the nine-time All-Star while he was still finding his place in Denver's rotation. Although Watson has undoubtedly improved by leaps and bounds, there is reason to believe that he would still struggle against the veteran.

As challenging as guarding Irving was, the nine-time All-Star was far from being the first major challenge he faced as a defender. That honor was reserved for Michael Porter Jr., whom Peyton Watson admittedly struggled against in his first matchup with the forward.

"I remember the first night we met each other; you [Porter Jr.] invited me out to Mizu in Denver," Watson began. "We had a good dinner. And I remember, the next day, I was flying to L.A., and you were flying somewhere else, but you were like, 'I wanted to get in the gym tomorrow before my flight, but my flight's early.' I said, 'Me too.' And you said, 'Let's just get in the gym at 6 AM.'"

"We went to the gym; we shot a little bit. I remember my manager came; he rebounded for us, we shot a little bit, and then we started playing one-on-one. I remember thinking in my head, 'I know he's the guy. I know he starts for our team. I'm about to come in this gym and get on his a–.' I remember that s–t like it was yesterday. And I came into that gym, and you tore my a– up."

During his tenure with the Denver Nuggets, Michael Porter Jr. primarily served as an off-ball and perimeter threat. However, this doesn't take away from his reputation as an elite scorer. Hence, when facing the forward, Peyton Watson received a brutal reality check but also learned a valuable lesson.

The matchup with Porter Jr. set the tone for Peyton Watson's development, as the 23-year-old revealed how it inspired him to focus on training and improvement. When you consider that he averaged 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.0 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game in his first season as a key starter for the Nuggets, his efforts certainly paid off.

These experiences will prove worthwhile now that Peyton Watson begins a new chapter in his career. Since he is likely to be a vital piece in Cleveland's starting lineup , the Cavaliers will hope the 23-year-old can step up and contribute to winning.

articles.title: Texas Tech’s Joey McGuire Takes Subtle Shot at USC Crowd After Lincoln Riley’s Program Forced to Take Action
articles.summary: Joey McGuire was careful with his words. Well, sort of.
articles.body:
Joey McGuire was careful with his words. Well, sort of. The Texas Tech coach said he respects USC and Lincoln Riley, then immediately flexed about 60,000 fans showing up in the Texas heat. The comparison was obvious, and USC's empty seats were clearly the target.

"Not to take any shots because I have a lot of respect for USC and Lincoln-Riley," Joey McGuire said via FOX College Football . "But, man, it's really awesome to be playing in Lubbock, Texas, knowing we're going to be playing in front of 60,000 and it's going to be warm."

He did not stop there. His next words sounded even more like a jab at USC fans who stayed away because of the heat. The No. 14 Trojans opened their 2026 season Saturday with a 42-26 victory over San Jose State, but the empty seats around the Coliseum became a story of their own.

"The great thing is, we've got some really tough people in West Texas that love their football, and they're going to show up no matter what the weather's like," he added. "There's not going to be any excuse for why they're not going to be here for us."

Lincoln Riley probably did not need that reminder. USC had already taken heat for the scene in Los Angeles, where the school announced an attendance of 51,144 in a Coliseum that holds 77,500. The empty seats were obvious, especially around kickoff.

Still, the weather was brutal. It was 94° when the game started, the heat index reportedly reached 110°, and Los Angeles was under an extreme-heat advisory. With barely any shade inside the Coliseum, staying away was not exactly a crazy decision.

The fans who did show up said the place was miserable, comparing the seats to hot plates and the Coliseum to a sauna. USC tried to manage it with cooling stations, fans, and relaxed water rules, but none of that fixed the optics.

The announced attendance of 51,144 was USC's lowest under Lincoln Riley and its lowest home figure since 2018. The school later acknowledged the poor turnout, with extreme heat, a noon kickoff, and limited shade among the major factors.

"We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season," the athletic department said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports. "We know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program."

Joey McGuire, meanwhile, is expecting no such problem when Texas Tech hosts Abilene Christian on Sept. 5 at the 60,229-seat Galaxy Stadium. The game kicks off at 6 p.m. CT, and Texas Tech has already sold out its primary ticket inventory.

That is why Joey McGuire feels good about the turnout. In Lubbock, Red Raiders football is the main event. Abilene Christian also brings back a nerve-rattling memory. Everyone remembers that Texas Tech needed overtime to win 52-51 in 2024.

Joey McGuire says USC wasn't his target. Still, after the Coliseum's attendance became a talking point, boasting about a packed house in Lubbock had a bit of a sting to it.

articles.title: From Mulvane to the NFL: Jayden Price makes Saints’ 53-man roster
articles.summary: After multiple practice squad stints and a year in the Canadian Football League and the United Football League, Price finally found a home in New Orleans and...
articles.body:
WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — From Mulvane High School to the NFL, former all-state quarterback Jayden Price made the New Orleans Saints' 53-man roster over the weekend.

After multiple practice squad stints and a year in the Canadian Football League and the United Football League, Price finally found a home in New Orleans and is in position to make his NFL debut this season.

He said it's been a long journey, but if you have a dream, go chase it.

"Doesn't matter how big of a school, how little of a school," Price said. "Doesn't matter how big of a town, how little of a town. Just that when you trust the process, you work hard, you do the right things and you can play football, then they'll find you."

Price was a three-year starter at Mulvane High School, playing quarterback and defensive back. He was recruited to North Dakota State as a cornerback. He appeared in 71 games and helped the Bison win three FCS championships.

He said the support he has received from his hometown over the years means the world.

"Just trying to set a good example for those young kids in that town and trying to make them proud and make that town proud," Price said. "And giving them something to look forward to and kind of be more thankful that they have my back."

Throughout his career, Price never forgot his roots. He's still close to his high school coach Dave Fennewald and former teammates.

Fennewald is now the athletics director at Mulvane High School, and he got to be in Dallas to watch Price's last game on the reserve list.

"We were driving back yesterday, and his mom texted me that head coach had text him and called him and said, 'You made the team,' and I was at home at that time, and I did I teared up," Fennewald said. "You just can't put that in words."

Fennewald said Price's character is what made him stand out and made the others around him better.

"If he came into school right now, you would never know he played for the NFL team," he said. "You wouldn't know. He'd walk around just like a normal kid."

Fennewald said that he has no doubt Price will take advantage of this opportunity with the Saints.

"He ain't done yet. He's not," he said. "He's going to make an impact someplace, some way on that team. He's going to make an impact."

Price's first shot to see the turf on an NFL Sunday will be against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 13.
