articles.title: Top performers for Monroe County Region sports on Monday, Aug. 31
articles.summary: A exchange student scores four times for Milan's soccer team against Airport; Erie Mason volleyball knocks off Summerfield and other local sports.
articles.body:
German exchange student Livius Guellmeister made an immediate impression on his new friends and teammates at Milan High School by scoring four goals in a 9-1 soccer victory over Airport on Monday, Aug. 31.

"It was a wonderful debut," Milan coach Phil Hayes said. "His plane just arrived on Friday. He had some good bonding with his teammates over the weekend."

Hayes knew Guellmeister was coming, but could not get here until after the Big Reds had played their first five games of the season.

"He's played a lot of soccer," the coach said. "I don't know what level, though."

Guellmeister's level was very high Monday, scoring nearly half of his team's goals.

Robert Gill added a goals and Wyatt Hurd came out of the goal to convert a penalty kick in the season half.

Other goals for the 3-2-1 Big Reds came from Tanner Lambers and Andrew Cruz.

Airport opened the scoring in the opening 30 seconds when Adam Ortega converted a pass from freshman Wyatt Sanders.

"That definitely caught up off guard," Hayes said. "It was a wake-up call. Sometimes you need a wake-up call."

Unfortunately for Airport, the young Jets could not follow up on that wake-up call.

"We only have 11 boys," coach Nick Suarez said. "We graduated 11 seniors form last year's team, which had our best record. It's tough to lose that many.

"This was a 2-1 game through the first 25 minutes. With our lack of depth, we are not an 80-minute team right now. We have some good sixth, seventh and eighth-graders. We knew this year would be rough."

Carson Welker, SMCC : Tallied three goals and an assist to spark a 7-0 win over Flat Rock. Aaron Fowkes, Spencer Schumate and Carson Peters each recorded a goal and assist and Stephen Ban picked up his first varsity goal. Ben Chavous posted the shutout with Aidan Cronin leading the defense.

Nathan Seisdedos-Henninger, New Boston Huron : Led a balanced attack with two goals in 7-0 win over Jefferson-Erie Mason. Matthew Hussey, Gonzalo Aragon and Parker Krause all finished with a goal and an assist. Marcos Reyna and Maverik Bazzy netted the other goals and Marton Krajcz and Dominic Lividini were credited with assists. Todd Elliott recorded the shutout. Jackson Vallie turned aside 32 shots for 1-2 Jefferson-Mason.

Trey Heaton, State Line Christian : Opened his junior season with a hat trick during an 8-0 victory over Pittsford Freedom Christian. Austin Nowak added a pair of goals, JR Hobbins rang up three assists and Steve Callejas notched a shutout in his first start in goal.

Addie Homrich, Erie Mason : Racked up 13 kills in a 25-12, 22-25, 25-14, 25-20 triumph over Summerfield. "The team showed great energy, teamwork, and determination throughout the match," Mason coach Kayle Scott said. "It was a strong start to the season." articles.title: NBA Reporter Calls Out Jonathan Kuminga’s Agent After Claims on Being Hawks’ Best Player
articles.summary: Another interview from Jonathan Kuminga’s agent has put his client back under the microscope. Aaron Turner has spent much of the offseason defending the deci...
articles.body:
Another interview from Jonathan Kuminga's agent has put his client back under the microscope. Aaron Turner has spent much of the offseason defending the decisions surrounding JK's free agency. At first, he explained why the former Warriors forward passed on more lucrative opportunities and eventually chose the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Now, Turner is defending Kuminga's brief run with the Atlanta Hawks. This time, however, his argument has drawn a sharp statistical rebuttal from NBA reporter Brett Siegel. Speaking on The Kevin O'Connor Show, Turner made a bold claim about Kuminga's impact after he was traded from Golden State to Atlanta.

"He was their best player from the moment that he showed up in terms of winning impact," Turner said on the Kevin O'Connor show. "He had the best on/off net rating, in the regular season and in the playoffs. In their two wins against the Knicks, who had the best net rating? These are not opinions, these are facts. Who had the best net rating? Jonathan Kuminga."

The clips from the show have become viral on social media, and it reached Siegel's timeline , who offered a much less flattering picture.

"From the time he was traded from the Warriors to the Hawks through the end of the regular season, Jonathan Kuminga ranked 6th on the Hawks in plus-minus. He ranked 5th in total net rating from Feb 24 through the end of the regular season and 9th on the team in the playoffs."

JK ranked sixth on the team in total plus-minus. His +100 mark was well behind Dyson Daniels, who led the Hawks at +300. The sample size matters, too. Jonathan Kuminga only played 16 regular-season games with Atlanta. He missed time after the trade because of injury before returning for the final stretch of the season.

That is hardly enough evidence to label him the team's best player confidently. Also, advanced statistics can tell very different stories when the sample is small.

Kuminga did help Atlanta win two games against the Knicks, and his offense was valuable in those contests. But several of his regular-season games also came late in the year, when some opponents were already focused on the lottery or resting key players. Using that stretch alone to establish Kuminga as Atlanta's best player is unfair to other Hawks stars.

The playoffs made that even clearer. Jonathan Kuminga averaged 13.7 points and 3.3 rebounds during Atlanta's six-game series against New York. He had productive performances in Games 2 and 3, but his overall efficiency remained inconsistent.

His three-point shooting throughout the series showed exactly why there are still questions about his offensive development. He went 0-for-2 from deep in Game 1, 1-for-4 in Game 2, 2-for-4 in Game 3, 0-for-6 in Game 4, and 1-for-5 in Game 5.

Then came Game 6. Kuminga finished with 11 points on 3-of-7 shooting, along with three assists and two rebounds in 23 minutes. The bigger problem was his -44 plus-minus, the worst mark on either team.

The bigger issue is that the discourse is no longer only about Kuminga's basketball ability. Turner has repeatedly found himself defending the decisions surrounding his client's career.

Last year, Turner and Kuminga reportedly turned down a three-year, $75 million structure from Golden State. This summer, Kuminga ultimately agreed to a two-year, roughly $12 million deal with Minnesota, including a player option for the second season.

Turner has argued that the decision was about maintaining flexibility and putting Kuminga in a better position to maximize his next opportunity. All the explanations have not stopped the criticism.

Former NBA player Ty Lawson was among those who reacted strongly , urging Kuminga to part ways with Turner after the interview.

"🤣😂🤣 Johnathan kuminga needs pack his agent up immediately.. send that 'you're fired' letter immediately… There's no way he jumped on camera like this lol."

At 23, Jonathan Kuminga has plenty of time to change and improve his game. Minnesota gives him another opportunity to prove what he can become.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka explains the Allen Iverson influence that plays a role in her career
articles.summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka discussed the influence that Allen Iverson has had on her career at the 2026 U. S.
articles.body:
Tennis star Naomi Osaka discussed the influence that Allen Iverson has had on her career at the 2026 U.S. Open.

Osaka is one of the most fashion-forward stars in the world of tennis right now, breathing life into the sport's pregame routine with audacious outfits reminiscent of NBA players coming out of the tunnel.

Turns out, that is one of the biggest reasons behind Osaka's dressing style, openly giving the credit to the legendary Allen Iverson for influencing her career.

Naomi Osaka looks up to the trailblazer Allen Iverson

Osaka spoke to the media before her first-round match against Anastasia Zakharova, discussing the impact that Iverson has had on her career by being an athlete involved in fashion.

"For me, he is a trailblazer. He's someone I look up to because he has done a lot in fashion, whether it was on purpose or not… I also think the conversation around clothes in sports and expressing yourself through style; I feel like he is someone I look up to in that regard."

Osaka wore an Allen Iverson-inspired outfit to her pre-tournament press conference, wearing a white sweatshirt with Iverson's image and a throwback 1997 cap for an Iverson-esque fit in 2026.

Iverson is considered to be the figure who truly brought pop culture into the NBA.

Ever since Iverson's rise in the early 2000s, the NBA started setting fashion trends through their biggest superstars rather than just following the lead of the entertainment world.

Iverson made fashion and pop culture synonymous with the NBA, and now Osaka hopes to do the same in the world of tennis.

The much stricter WTA dress code might not allow Osaka the same freedom Iverson had to show off his style, but the 28-year-old American tennis star is maximising the opportunities when she can show off her style.

articles.title: Oregon vs Boise State Prediction: Just How Good Are These Ducks?
articles.summary: It's a College Football Playoff-level matchup as Boise State travels to Oregon. How strong is this year's Duck team? We'll find out fast. Here's the CFN prev...
articles.body:
Oregon is No. 2 in the major polls, it's expected to be knee-deep in the national title hunt, and yes, this really might be the most talented Duck team in the program's history. But Boise State isn't a program that gets fazed by such things. The newest member of the Pac-12 also has big dreams coming into the season as one of the favorites to take the Group of Six spot in the College Football Playoff.

The series history is 3-1, and probably not in the way you would think. Boise State took the first three meetings before Oregon slipped by in a 37-34 fight to start the 2024 season.

Boise State has lost four of its last five season openers after winning six in a row.

Oregon has to travel to Oklahoma State next as it preps for the start of the Big Ten season at USC in late September. Boise State hosts Memphis next week in a huge showdown of Group of Six teams.

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 pm ET TV: CBS Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – CFN Week 1 Schedule, Predictions

This is a better Boise State team than last year's version. Quarterback Maddux Madsen is back and healthy, the offensive line is a major plus, and the defensive line has the edge rushers to bring the heat on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore. Oregon's pass rush will be fine, but it wasn't anything special last season and needs to get to Madsen on a regular basis. The Broncos have the potential to control the tempo with short to midrange passes to keep the chains moving. – Boise State 2026 Preview

Can the Boise State defense really hold up against a top offense? Overall, it'll be statistically terrific, but over the last few years it's had a problem producing against the attacks with talent. Washington, Fresno State, Notre Dame, and USF all worked just fine last season against the Broncos, and this Oregon offense should be at a whole other level from those four. But it'll be the other side that should be the bigger problem, with the loaded Duck secondary forcing Madsen to try making the deep plays. Fernando Mendoza was the only quarterback to complete 60% of his passes against Oregon last season. Boise State didn't get to 60% in nine games. – Oregon 2026 Preview

Oregon vs Boise State Prediction, Betting Lines

Oregon will come out roaring, and it won't stop. Boise State might have the experience and upside to get tough like it did two years ago in the good three-point loss, but this year's Duck team is stronger. Moore will be razor-sharp from the start, but it'll be the running game that takes over and shows why this is the nation's No. 2 team.

articles.title: Bryson Stott hits a solo HR, Phillies beat the Diamondbacks 2-1 to cap 21-win August
articles.summary: Bryson Stott hit a homer, Aaron Nola provided another solid start on the mound and the Philadelphia Phillies finished a torrid August with a 2-1 victory over...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Bryson Stott hit a homer, Aaron Nola provided another solid start on the mound and the Philadelphia Phillies finished a torrid August with a 2-1 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Monday night.

The Phillies have won five straight, 14 of their past 16 and finished with a 21-7 record in August, which was the best mark in the big leagues. They're now just four games behind the Atlanta Braves in the NL East.

Stott crushed a 464-foot homer to right field in the second that gave the Phillies a 1-0 lead. Bryce Harper's double off the center field wall in the third scored Garrett Stubbs and pushed the advantage to 2-0.

Nola (6-10) pitched into the sixth inning, giving up one run on five hits and two walks, striking out five. The veteran right-hander has given up two runs or less in five straight starts.

Alex McFarlane, Orion Kerkering, Brooks Raley, Jose Alvarado and Jhoan Duran combined for four scoreless innings of relief. Duran earned his 29th save in 31 chances, stranding runners on first and third.

Three-time All-Star Ketel Marte made his return for the Diamondbacks , two weeks after he failed to show up for a game in Boston. He was the designated hitter, batted cleanup and was 1 for 3 at the plate with a single and a walk.

The D-backs cut the deficit to 2-1 in the bottom of the third when Geraldo Perdomo scored all the way from first on Gabriel Moreno's double down the left field line.

Arizona is now a half-game behind the San Diego Padres for the third and final NL wild card.

D-backs right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-2) gave up two runs on five hits and a walk over six innings, striking out one.

The D-backs send LHP Eduardo Rodriguez (14-4, 2.50 ERA) to the mound on Tuesday night to face Phillies LHP Jesus Luzardo (12-5, 3.09).

articles.title: Stephen Curry Shuts Down Warriors Exit Rumors Amid $136.7 Million Extension Woes; Reconfirms Retirement Plan
articles.summary: Stephen Curry puts an end to all exit speculations by reconfirming his plan to retire with the Warriors.
articles.body:
There has been a lot of speculation about Stephen Curry's future with the Warriors ever since reports claimed their front office is now focusing on the post-Steph era in Golden State. But the 38-year-old Warriors superstar has reassured their fans that he's not going anywhere.

Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry , recently spoke to Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports and clarified that the rumors are not true, but smartly sidestepped why he's delaying the contract extension despite being eligible for a two-year, $136.7 million deal .

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen. The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

"Hopefully we can be healthy and just have a chance to show what we're capable of, myself included, missing so many games last year. So, yeah, the goal stays the same. I want to be here. The extension stuff, we'll figure that out at the right time."

"But I'm ready for year 18. It's kind of crazy that it's been this long, and I'm still trying to play at a very high level to help us win, and I'll be able to do my job," Curry concluded .

This should put to rest all the exit rumors that had started popping up ever since the Warriors missed out on the LeBron James sweepstakes . But while Johnson had asked Stephen Curry if he plans to sign this season, saying that he's waiting for 'the right time' only suggests that he's only waiting to be eligible for a three-year extension as a free agent next summer.

Still, there is no certainty on whether Curry will sign that extension deal this summer, as he would become eligible for a contract extension exceeding $200 million in the summer of 2027. But what is certain is that he will stay with the Warriors and does not plan to go anywhere.

The next big question is: how long will Stephen Curry continue playing, now that he turned 38 this year? Johnson asked Ayesha Curry whether her husband, Stephen Curry, has multiple seasons left.

"Of course, Steph is the hardest-working man in the room. He has no days off. He hasn't stopped since last season ended. He's ready. He's ready to get out there. I think we're going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years," she said.

Curry is still playing at a high level but spent most of last season on the bench while suffering from runner's knee. He ended 2025-26 averaging 26.6 points, 4.7 assists, and 3.6 rebounds while shooting 46.8% from the field and 39.3% from behind the three-point line.

So if Stephen Curry is waiting until the summer of 2027 to sign a three-year deal, that means he plans to play until the summer of 2030, when he would have turned 42. But Curry said last season that he is looking at his career in two-year phases, so he may not have planned that far ahead to 2030.

It might turn out he only signs a two-year extension, as he is eligible for. But one thing is certain: his contract extension is now a question of when, not if.

articles.title: Angels end 7-game slide with 10-1 win over sloppy Yankees behind Grissom and Ureña
articles.summary: Vaughn Grissom drove in four runs, rookie Walbert Ureña pitched seven strong innings and the Los Angeles Angels ended a seven-game losing streak with a 10-1...
articles.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. (AP) — Vaughn Grissom drove in four runs, rookie Walbert Ureña pitched seven strong innings and the Los Angeles Angels ended a seven-game losing streak with a 10-1 victory over the sloppy New York Yankees on Monday night.

Mike Trout had a two-run single and Christian Moore drove in a pair of runs as the Angels won at home for the first time since Aug. 15. Ureña (9-9) gave up five hits with no walks and eight strikeouts.

Elmer Rodríguez (0-3) failed to make it out of the fourth for the Yankees, allowing four runs and four hits with three walks over 3 2/3 innings. It was the shortest of his six career starts since making his major league debut in April.

Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who committed three errors after scoring a combined 25 runs in consecutive wins over the rival Boston Red Sox at home last weekend. New York is three games ahead of Boston for the top American League wild card and 4 1/2 games behind first-place Tampa Bay in the AL East.

The Angels took a 1-0 lead in the third on Grissom's run-scoring single. Zach Neto had an RBI single in the fourth after both Oswald Peraza and Tyler Heineman were hit by pitches from Rodríguez with two outs.

Trout added his two-run single in the fourth for his first multi-RBI hit since a two-run homer on July 8.

Jones connected in the fifth to make it 4-1.

Moore had a bloop RBI double in the bottom of the fifth and scored on an errant pickoff throw to second by Michael Fulmer. Neto scored in the sixth for a 7-1 lead when Yankees shortstop José Caballero made two errors on what could have been an inning-ending double-play grounder by Grissom.

In the eighth, Grissom made it 9-1 with a two-run double off the wall in left field and Moore added an RBI single. Grissom finished with three hits and scored twice.

Yankees RHP Gerrit Cole (7-3, 3.19 ERA) faces Angels RHP Grayson Rodriguez (4-5, 6.03) in the middle game of the series Tuesday.

articles.title: Yankees call out Red Sox radio voice for suggesting beaning for late stolen bases
articles.summary: Several New York Yankees are taking exception to comments made by Boston Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming during a weekend series between the rivals.  J...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Several New York Yankees are taking exception to comments made by Boston Red Sox radio announcer Will Flemming during a weekend series between the rivals.

Jazz Chisholm Jr. was among the players who called out Flemming on Monday after the WEEI radio announcer called the second baseman a "bush league player" for stealing two bases with the Yankees leading 7-1 in the eighth inning of Sunday's series finale .

Chisholm and several teammates also called out Flemming for suggesting Red Sox pitcher Jovani Moran retaliate by beaning Yankees catcher Austin Wells.

"They're called unwritten rules because you're not really breaking any rules," Chisholm told reporters before Monday's game against the Los Angeles Angels. "You've seen teams — actually them — do the same thing where they're pouring on runs. We didn't have nothing to say or nothing to do about it. That's just showing how unprofessional he is."

Flemming apologized on social media for what he said during the telecast.

"Since I have been receiving nonstop calls and threats, I felt like it was important to hop back on here and say: My comments during yesterday's broadcast crossed a line. I'm emotional and a fan at heart and that bled into the broadcast," Flemming posted. "I meant no disrespect to the Yankees players or organization. I could and should have used different words. These rivalry games get me fired up; I apologize for letting the emotion of the moment get the best of me."

articles.title: Commanders get some good news at Monday's practice
articles.summary: Washington was back on the practice field Monday, and so were some key players that were dealing with injuries.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and, on Monday, made two more moves , transferring Laremy Tunsil and Johnny Newton to the injured reserve. After moving Tunsil and Newton to IR with the designation to return, Washington re-signed cornerback Fabian Moreau and defensive tackle Shy Tuttle.

The Commanders returned to practice for the first time since finalizing their roster, and there was some good news. Center Nick Allegretti, quarterback, tight end Ben Sinnott, and defensive tackle Daron Payne were back at practice on Monday.

Allegretti's return is most notable given concerns about the center position. He missed virtually all of training camp after moving over from guard this offseason. Head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters are not concerned about Allegretti.

"So, not having Nick for most of camp was something we had to work through, but we have a ton of confidence in him," Peters said. "And he's played, I think 3,000-some-odd snaps in this league. And he's played good football for us before. He went through the whole offseason, so we're really confident. He's not a guy that needs a ton of reps, especially from a mental standpoint."

Allegretti strained his calf on the first day of training camp, which highlighted Washington's depth concerns at center. Those concerns were exacerbated one week later when star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps. That move had a domino effect on the line, forcing Brandon Coleman, who was competing to start at left guard, back to left tackle.

Mariota sprained his MCL in the preseason opener, but the prognosis was always that he'd be ready for Week 1. Sinnott was injured late in camp, while Payne was dealing with an undisclosed injury.

Washington opens the season in 13 days on the road at Philadelphia.

articles.title: Driver born with no arms looking to make motorsport history
articles.summary: Callum Smith is set to test his specially-adapted race car at Donnington Park for the first time.
articles.body:
A driver born with no arms says he is determined to make motorsport history by competing at the highest levels - using only his feet.

Callum Smith from Warwickshire learned to drive just two years ago but has now joined Team Brit, a competitive team of disabled racing drivers.

The team has adapted a BMW 1 Series specifically for the driver, who has been passionate about motorsports since childhood.

"My motto in life has always been improvise, adapt and overcome," he said.

His passion was spotted by the all-disabled team which signed him as a rookie driver after a successful test day at Silverstone.

Smith, from Nuneaton, will get his first opportunity to test the adapted car at Donnington Park on 2 September.

The 23-year-old said he had spent his life adapting to everyday challenges.

"I grew up learning to use my feet to do everything," he said.

"I've always believed that if I put my mind to something, I can achieve it.

"Now, fast forward to today, and we're getting ready for my first test in a race car."

Team Brit was established in 2015 and evolved from a charity that provided karting opportunities for disabled armed forces personnel.

Principal Mike Scudamore said it quickly escalated from just one car "back in the day" to four vehicles and eight drivers.

"The most exciting thing about our racing is that there's no class for disability, so we race against able-bodied people all over the UK," Scudamore said.

"Team Brit's ultimate goal is to be the first all-disabled team to race in the world-famous Le Mans 24 hours.

"There have been a couple of disabled drivers that have had a go, but not one team with all their drivers having a disability and we can't wait to try and been the first people to do that."

Smith's race car has been adapted by Coventry company Jim Doran Hand Controls.

They had initially adapted Smith's own car, then were asked if they would consider doing the same for a race car.

Director Dan Doran said: "Callum obviously came to us as a young lad and really didn't really know what adaptions were out there."

Once he was shown the foot steering he knew it was the right thing for him, he said.

For the adapted car "we've basically put the steering wheel on the floor.

"[We've] moved his pedals over a bit and Callum will use his left foot to steer the car and his right foot to operate the brake and accelerator."

"All of us, me and the lads in the workshop, are all excited to help Callum on his journey."

Despite all the adaptations to his car, there are still difficulties for the rookie to overcome before he can become a full-time driver with the team.

To get a licence to compete on the track, Smith will have to prove he can get out of the car unaided in 10 seconds.

But he is determined not to be held back.

"Once I set my mind to something, I'm going to do it," he said.

"This is just another challenge that I'm willing to conquer."

There is also a financial hurdle to overcome - he will need to raise £50,000 to cover the cost of the car conversion, equipment and tuition costs.

So, like many new racing drivers, he is looking for sponsors.

articles.title: Wawrinka feels the love on Grand Slam goodbye
articles.summary: Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka is given an emotional send-off at the US Open following the final Grand Slam match of his career.
articles.body:
Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka felt the love at the US Open after being given an emotional send-off following the final Grand Slam match of his career.

The 41-year-old Swiss is retiring at the end of the season and looked close to tears as he received a rapturous reception after a straight-set defeat by Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Wawrinka, who won the US Open in 2016, was initially overlooked by tournament organisers for a wildcard, but was given a last-minute reprieve following American recipient Patrick Kypson's withdrawal.

The belated decision can be considered well justified given the thousands who packed into the 8,000-capacity Grandstand court at Flushing Meadows.

Wawrinka made heart gestures with his fingers, and put his hand on his heart, at the end of an enjoyable contest to illustrate his appreciation.

With huge cheers already ringing his ears, the former world number three encouraged the crowd to make more noise before knocking balls into the stands as souvenirs of the occasion.

"One of the reasons I played until 41 was to live these moments," said Wawrinka, who also won the Australian Open in 2014 and the French Open in 2015.

"I'm very grateful for this wildcard. It was very important for me to finish here, where I won a Grand Slam 10 years ago. I want to thank you all for all these years."

Wawrinka was only given the news about the wildcard on Wednesday, when he was back in the Swiss mountains having travelled home from New York two days earlier.

Despite the late notice he quickly rearranged a return across the Atlantic in order to play at one of his most loved venues for the final time.

Fans arrived early and waited in long queues to ensure they could witness what they knew could be his Grand Slam goodbye.

It turned out that way as 2021 Wimbledon finalist Berrettini made his veteran opponent pay for not taking his chances.

Wawrinka held set points in each of the first two sets - one in the first and three more in the second - but Berrettini fought them off before running away with the third set.

Berrettini led the applause before Wawrinka addressed the crowd and received a photo montage of his US Open triumph from chief executive Craig Tiley.

Afterwards Wawrinka - celebrated for his one-handed backhand and competitive spirit - said he was "super grateful" for the fond farewell.

"It's showed me that I did the right thing all those 20 years by always trying to fight, always showing up, always trying to do my best, and always trying to push myself to the limits," he added.

"This is what for me was the most important thing - what I get from the fans when I play."
